copy.title: Series pitch: comps
copy.body: Bottom of the Ninth is a mockumentary workplace comedy about the front office of the worst minor-league baseball team in America, which has one season to sell 3,000 tickets or move to a casino parking lot. It draws on the same audience as Ted Lasso, Abbott Elementary, Parks and Recreation and Bull Durham. Closest comps are Jury Duty Presents (fit 0.99, Mid-list, Top 5%) for the docu-comedy, talking-head format and Reservation Dogs (fit 0.91, Niche, Top 10%) for deadpan tone and emotional engagement. Players (fit 0.88) shows the sports, coach and heartfelt lane is already being served, and Reboot (fit 0.98) and Rutherford Falls (fit 0.97) show strong taste overlap in smaller workplace and satire comedies. Every comp is from 2020 or later, so the lane is current. The audience over-indexes at 35–44 (+0.18) and 55+ (+0.10), with a near-even gender split. Taste descriptors include satire, office, dark comedy and job. Emerging markets include Louisville, Washington DC, Burlington, Atlanta, Portland and Albuquerque. Affinity describes aggregate taste, not results. [word count]

copy.title: Who it's for
copy.body: The audience skews toward 35–44 (+0.18) and 55+ (+0.10) and under-indexes at 30–34 (-0.56). Gender is effectively even. Their taste runs to satire, office and dark comedy, with New York City, restaurant and domestic drama in the mix. Beyond TV, they also love Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story, Champions and Hot Rod in film, and podcasts like Staying In with Emily & Kumail and 2 Dope Queens. Their music taste includes Paul Simon and John Prine. Brands in their orbit include New York Yankees and Nike. Emerging markets are Louisville, Washington DC, Burlington, Atlanta, Portland and Albuquerque.

kit.headline: Ted Lasso and Abbott Elementary warmth with Parks and Recreation workplace mechanics and the Bull Durham minor-league ballpark, told as a mockumentary in the lane Jury Duty Presents opened.
kit.summary: Bottom of the Ninth sits between the mockumentary comedies and the sports-underdog comedies this audience already loves. It is for viewers who over-index at 35–44 and 55+, with a taste for satire, office comedy and dark comedy. Lead with Jury Duty Presents meets Reservation Dogs for format and tone, and use Players as the sports proof point. Fit is aggregate taste, not a forecast.
